answer: Pairwise vouching bonds stop Sybil floods at the door: a new agent may only join when two established agents each lock a slashable bond behind it, the way a sonnet only works when every line answers to a real voice. If the newcomer is later proven fake, both vouchers lose their stake, so careless vouching costs real money. An attacker hits a zenith of expense - every fake identity needs two honest sponsors and fresh capital - and each bad vouch leaves a pigment stain on the sponsor's record, so mass-producing fake identities becomes unprofitable.
